description: The Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level (PSMSL) is the global data bank for long-term sea level change information from tide gauges and bottom pressure recorders. It publishes mean sea level records for stations around the world in two sets, Revised Local Reference (RLR) and Metric, whose differences are explained in its help file. Coverage: global coastlines, with records at some stations reaching back to the nineteenth century; an end-of-year data release is made annually (the latest listed is the end of 2025 release), and records updated in the 60 days before 21 September 2026 are flagged. Format and access: station pages with data files and plots, a map-based data explorer, the complete dataset, year-end archives, notes on formats and links to the ellipsoid for stations with GNSS; free. Licence: not stated as a licence; users are asked to cite the latest data paper (Holgate et al., 2013) and the dataset. Caveats: users must check which of the RLR and Metric sets suits their analysis; the site also runs a data rescue project for historical records. Simulation uses: relative sea level trends at the coast for sea level rise and coastal flood exposure of ports, power stations, transport and water infrastructure. Related records: the Environment Agency flood monitoring API (data-uk-ea-real-time-flood-monitoring-api) provides real-time tide gauge readings in England.
